title: Randomization preserves the second moment norm
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, and let $f$ be real-valued on its outcome space. The second moment norm of the randomized expansion, averaging over outcomes under $P$ and uniform Boolean sign vectors, equals the second moment norm of $f$: $\|Rf\|_{2}=\|f\|_{2,P}$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is a real-valued function on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $(\mathbb E_{x\sim P}\mathbb E_r|\sum_S\chi_S(r)f_S(x)|^2)^{1/2}=\|f\|_{2,P}$, where $r$ is uniform on the Boolean cube. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$.
